title: Four-panel developmental comparison: zebrafish and flying fish, with and without enlarged paired fins
status: Panels A to C rest on real data; panel D is HYPOTHESIS ONLY. Nothing here is a flying-fish genetic experiment, because none exists. A flying fish's wing is an enlarged pectoral fin, so this is about fin proportion, not about a fin becoming a wing.
the_two_limits_of_this_comparison: The zebrafish side has no number on the flying fish's axis. No fetched source measures pectoral fin length over standard length in a wild-type zebrafish, and every measurement of the winged zebrafish lives in a figure panel. So the 2x2 cannot be drawn to one scale: the zebrafish panels are qualitative and the flying-fish panels are quantitative.

Only one of the four panels is an experiment. Panel B is a real germline double heterozygote. Panel C is a morphometric series. Panel A is a baseline that was never measured on this axis, and panel D is an animal that does not exist.

phenotype.value_status: NOT MEASURED IN ANY FETCHED SOURCE
phenotype.note: No fetched source reports pectoral fin length over standard length for a wild-type zebrafish. The only wild-type zebrafish fin measurement this thread holds is caudal lepidotrichial segment length, 290.7 +/- 32.7 micrometres (n = 10 fin rays), which is a different quantity on a different fin. So panel A cannot be placed on the same axis as panels C and D, and the comparison is qualitative on the zebrafish side.
phenotype.what_is_known: caudal ray segment length 290.7 +/- 32.7 um (n=10 rays), wild type, from the connexin literature

panels.role: the real experiment, and the closest thing to a made flying fish

genotype.description: trans-heterozygote of two dominant alleles: lat4a nr21 (ZFIN slc43a2a, allele dmh26, a T200K substitution in a conserved domain of the L-type amino acid transporter, on chromosome 15) together with kcnh2a lof (the classic longfin dt2 allele, a chromosome-2 inversion that leaves both coding regions intact and places the prrx1a regulatory region upstream of the kcnh2a transcription start site, so kcnh2a is ectopically expressed in fins)
alleles: lat4a nr21 / + (dmh26, T200K, gain of function)
genotype.level: one coding and one cis-regulatory, in combination
genotype.germline_note: Both are germline alleles carried in the fish line, so the perturbation is present from fertilisation, which is what 'from the beginning of development' requires. Note the contrast with the same paper's sufficiency experiment, which injected a HUMAN KCNH2 transgene to make somatic mosaic clones: that one is NOT germline and is a different experiment.
genotype.gain_of_function_evidence: lat4a nr21 is a gain of function, shown by reversion: CRISPR frameshifts made in cis to the nr21 allele revert the fin phenotype to wild type, and fish lacking lat4a altogether have no fin phenotype.

figure_panels: Figures S2A and S2B lepidotrichial segments
phenotype.note: The measurement exists but only as a figure panel: no numeric value for it appears anywhere in the paper's text, legends or Data S1, whose fourteen sheets are comparative genomics and beloniform specimen measurements, with no zebrafish sheet. Not digitised here.

qualitative_in_the_papers_words.caudal_fin: generally wild type in size but hypocercal, with an elongated ventral lobe
qualitative_in_the_papers_words.segments: regular segmentation is maintained, unlike the kcnk5b overgrowth mutant whose segmentation is irregular

single_mutants_for_contrast.lat4a nr21 / + alone: all fins shortened, and lepidotrichial segments shorter
single_mutants_for_contrast.lat4a nr21 body size: NOT reduced: the paper states the mutant 'does not have a statistically decreased body size', so the fin change is allometric, not a change in overall growth

phenotype.why_this_panel_matters: The non-additivity is the result: two dominant alleles that each change all fins combine to change the fins DIFFERENTLY from each other, leaving medial fins wild type while the paired fins stay overgrown. That fin-type-specific outcome is what resembles a flying fish, not the size change alone.

stage_of_perturbation.acts_from: fertilisation (both alleles are in the germline)
stage_of_perturbation.when_phenotype_is_scored: adult; the fin measurements and the images are of adult fish

panels.evidence_grade: mechanism for the interaction (reversion, in-cis CRISPR, qRT-PCR showing kcnh2a expression is unchanged by nr21, so lat4a acts downstream rather than through kcnh2a levels)

the_papers_own_claim.quote: The overall fin phenotype of the kcnh2alof;lat4anr21 fish is thus remarkably similar to that of flying fishes, suggesting the interaction between these two genes is sufficient to phenocopy this key innovation and organismal bauplan of flying fishes (Figure 4).

sources.quote: Interestingly, double mutants between kcnh2alof/+ and lat4anr21/+ are viable and show specific, non-additive variation in proportion among fins: while all fins of kcnh2alof/+ are overgrown and all fins of lat4anr21/+ are shortened, the lat4anr21/+;kcnh2alof/+ fish show wild-type-sized medial fins, while the paired fins are overgrown (Figure 4).
Surprisingly, the caudal fin of kcnh2alof/+;lat4anr21/+, while generally wild type in size, is hypocercal, with an elongated ventral lobe.
The nr21 mutant, however, does not have a statistically decreased body size (Figure 3B).

panels.fin_state: enlarged pectoral fins, the real animal

genotype.description: UNKNOWN. No flying-fish genetic manipulation exists and no flying-fish functional genetics of any kind was found. What exists is comparative sequence evidence: a convergent F326L substitution in lat4a present in both gliding halfbeak genera and in at least 7 of 9 sequenced flying-fish species, and the kcnh2a locus implicated by the same phylogenomic analysis. Neither has been tested in any species.
alleles: lat4a F326L (convergent substitution, never engineered or assayed)

phenotype.value_status: MEASURED, by the Daane authors on museum specimens
phenotype.allometry_in_the_papers_words: the length of flying fish pectoral fins increases rapidly as the body grows, and the relationship is identical across two- and four-wing flying fishes

stage_of_perturbation.acts_from: the species' own development; nothing was perturbed
stage_of_perturbation.note: Specimens are preserved adults and juveniles across a 1.7 to 24 cm standard-length range; the smallest specimens have the lowest ratios, so the trait develops with size rather than being fixed.

panels.evidence_grade: measurement (not an experiment): a morphometric series, with the genetics only associated by comparative genomics

sources.note: Data S1A, sheet 'A - fin measurement'; re-tabulated by genotype/fin_ratios_table.py

panels.role: hypothetical; the panel with no genetics at all

genotype.description: HYPOTHESIS ONLY. No experiment has ever removed or reduced a flying fish's pectoral fins, and no flying-fish gene has been manipulated. Two routes are conceivable from the comparative evidence and neither has been tested in any organism: reverting the convergent lat4a F326L substitution to the ancestral residue, or reverting the kcnh2a regulatory state implicated by the phylogenomics. Both are labelled hypothesis and must not be presented as routes that are known to work.
alleles: kcnh2a regulatory state reverted (untested, and the regulatory lesion in flying fish is not even characterised)
genotype.germline: would have to be germline to act from the beginning of development, which is itself untested

phenotype.value_status: NOT OBSERVABLE: no such animal exists. The values below are its non-gliding RELATIVES, measured, and stand in for the phenotype.
phenotype.reading: Within the same order, pectoral fin length over standard length runs from about 0.088 in needlefishes and 0.14 in halfbeaks, through 0.274 in the two gliding halfbeak genera, to 0.687 in flying fishes. The gliding halfbeaks sit between the two, which is why the series reads as a graded trait rather than a switch. A 'wingless flying fish' would be expected to sit near the halfbeak end, but that is an inference from relatives, not a measurement of a flying fish.

stage_of_perturbation.acts_from: not applicable: no perturbation has been done

panels.evidence_grade: hypothesis for the genotype; measurement for the proxy phenotypes

sources.note: comparative series from Data S1A; the convergent substitution from sheet 'G - conv. aa subst.'

how_to_read_this: A figure-only measurement is reported as figure-only. Nothing was digitised from a plot.
Germline is stated per panel, because 'from the beginning of development' excludes the somatic mosaic experiments in the same paper.
The winged zebrafish is a trans-heterozygote of two DOMINANT alleles, so it is not a knockout of anything.
The interesting result in panel B is non-additivity between the two alleles, not the size change.
